description_text:
29-05-2021 The foundation parts are updated. The new STL files can be found in “NEW foundation parts.zip”
This Bird Feeder  has a build in lamp. The lamp sits in the feeder part and shins up. The Lamp is actually a RGB LED strip, so it can change colors also.I tried to make the feeder part in such a way that water can easily escape trough an build in channel. Because there is a lamp inside it's possible to take this one apart for fixing purposes in the future. In the center of the pillars sits a “translucent PET-G printed” cylinder (lamp glass roof.stl) wherein the IR receiver is placed. This way the remote can still be used :-). If you do not have a remote, you can also use this part to place a second lamp :-)
The position of the “ROOF PART with cable bore.stl” might be strange but works very good.
Printing details for people who like a guide line:
base.stl is printed with 30% infill and 4 wall, bottom & top lines/layers in PLAfoundation parts are printed with 10% infill and 4 wall, bottom & top lines/layers in PLAlamp glass or feeder part.stl is printed 25% infill, 3 wall lines, 3 Top layers & 2 bottom layers in PET-Glamp glass roof.stl is printed 25% infill, 2 wall lines, 3 Top layers & 2 bottom layers in PET-Gmount STL's are printed 35% infill and 4 wall, bottom & top lines/layers in PET-G Carbonthe pillars are printed 10% infill and 4 wall, bottom & top lines/layers in PLAthe roof parts are printed 10% infill and 4 wall, bottom & top lines/layers in PLAthe spikes are printed 20% infill and 4 wall, bottom & top lines/layers in PLA (the heat bed temp must kept as low as possible to prevent warping on the spiky tips/ends)
needed parts:1X base.stl1X foundation part with bore for cable to the baseA.stl1X foundation part with bore for cable to the baseB.stl2X foundation partA.stl2X foundation partB.stl1X lamp glass or feeder part.stl1X lamp glass roof.stl1X mount second peace.stl1X mount with bore.stl1X pillar with bore for cable to the base.stl3X pillar with mounting for base.stl2X pillar.stl6X ROOF PART with cable bore.stl6X spike foundation part.stl6X spike roof.stl6X M3x20mm bolt & nut (3 extra ones are optional for roof)1X M3x60mm bolt & nut (or 2 nuts and 60mm treated rod as I did)1X Lamp or LED to mount inside.Super Glue & Universal Glue for the base feeder part
If you have any questions, feel free to ask :-)
PS: for more information about this model go to https://www.designuitinspiratie.nl/3d-printer/verlichte-lucht-tempel/ on my personal website :-)

description_text:
third prize winner of the POLYMAKERCHALLENGE
This Ambient Lamp is inspired by the Lotus Flower.It consist out of 10 parts mainly to make it FDM printing ready. Print support is still necessary for the “center.stl”, “mid.stl” & the “bottom.stl” parts.The mid & bottom parts are printed in translucent Green PET-G and the center was printed in White PLA. The PLA is translucent enough :-) with the settings : 0.2mm layer hight, 0.8mm top/bottom thickness, 0.8mm wall thickness & 20% infill.Inside this example are 1 Red, 1 Green and 1 Blue LED. The bending of the light in the center part makes a Rainbow at the top of the Lamp. I tried to photograph it and succeeded a little bit. You can see it on one of the Pictures :-)Also the overall color of the lamp can change by dimming the LEDs individually.The dimensions of this Lamp Assembled are 142,16mm x 146,257mm and 72.18mm high.
Of course other Light sources can be used as long as it fits :-) The hole for the Light source (in the center part) has a radius of around 32mm (inside is egg shaped)
Also included is a exploded view of the Lamp. This makes it easier to see how it all comes together.
If you have questions, feel free to ask :-)

description_text:
The Resin Jar is a threaded jar, designed to hold 50 to 130ml of liquid (sizes 50ml, 75ml, 100ml, & 130ml).
This design seems to do a great job for temporary storage, for custom color mixing. Your average resin printer vat holds 100 to 130 ml. The jar should never be filled above the beginning of its narrowest point. The top threads into the narrow to create a nearly water tight seal. The seal depends greatly on the printer, the material and the settings used when printing. The inner lid has an indentation for the addition of a rubber band to enhance the seal. Best to store upright, avoiding potential leaks.
For resin storage, it is best to use opaque materials, black, dark colors, and deep reds, blocking out as much light as possible. I printed the tests on my FDM printer, but I may make a couple with the resin printer, sidestepping issues inherent problems with liquids.
While wood was used for some tests, the less exotic PLA had the best water tight surface in its base. Regardless, I'd suggest coating the interior with a thin layer of resin, curing it to better seal the layered interior. I've done so with the wooden PLA prints, making them useful for resin storage. Otherwise, they'd be good for storing powders, pills, thick gels, and paint.

description_text:
This Lamp began as a test Vase to be honest. I wanted to test a new printer and this “Vase” was one of the Test models I made. I liked it so much that I turned it into a Lamp. 
To do this I made a simple “ base “. There are 2. The one I used is “base 6mm.stl”, but If you want to scale down, “base 21mm.stl” might be better (In the “base” is a small cavity where the connector of the LED strip is housed. If you scale down the base to much, this cavity might become to small for the connector).The (in Translucent Blue PET-G) Printed Vase sits on this Base. Then in the Vase an Aluminum tube is bolted down using an M4x40 bolt, nut and printed parts “tube plug lamp.stl”. An LED strip (15meters) is wrapped around this tube, making the light source. To get a better the idea how this all comes together, please see the Photos in the Photo section.
The Aluminum tube I used is 490mm high and has an outer diameter of  34mm.The Lamp Shade (or Vase) is 558.7mm high. Yes I had to scale it down because there was not enough Filament on any Roll at the time :-) At 100% scale it is 705.871mm high.Note that the Lamp Shade (or Vase) is printed using the “Spiral Outer Contour” mode in Cura.The Nozzle I used is 0.8mm. With smaller Nozzle sizes the print will warp at this size.
So for most people its not going to work. I Also printed this model at 240mm high and it worked out super nice. For this small one I used a 0.4mm Nozzle.
Then I Also experimented with a “diffuser”. This is simply a cylinder that fits around the aluminum (with the LED strip) Tube. The Idea is to spread the light form the LEDs a bit better. Hoping the individual LEDs can not be spot trough the Lamp Shade (or Vase) anymore. I printed it in Translucent PET-G and it did not work very good. The LEDs still can be identified as individual light spots in the Lamp Shade. Maybe just white PLA will do a better job. But I just experimented with spray painting mine white. It works out, but more paint means less Light. The distance of the diffuser to the LEDs also is very important. If this distance is to short the diffuser also doesn't work.
Anyhow, You can make it as difficult as You want I guess. The simples way is to just print “giant vase2.stl” en the “base”. Put them together with a lamp of choice inside :-)
Feel free to ask any questions or constructive comments :-)

*Reflection in computer graphics is used to emulate reflective objects like mirrors and shiny surfaces.*Accurate reflections can be accomplished e.g. by a ray trace renderer by following a ray from the eye to the mirror and then calculating where it bounces from, and continuing the process until no surface is found, or a non-reflective surface is found. Approximate reflections can usually be computed faster by using methods such as environment mapping. Reflection on a shiny surface like wood or tile can add to the photorealistic effects of a 3D rendering.
**Diffuse reflection**Diffuse reflection is the reflection of light or other waves or particles from a surface such that a ray incident on the surface is scattered at many angles rather than at just one angle as in the 
case of specular reflection. An ideal diffuse reflecting surface is said to exhibit Lambertian reflection, meaning that there is equal luminance when viewed from all directions lying in the half-space adjacent to the surface.
A surface built from a non-absorbing powder such as plaster, or from fibers such as paper, or from a polycrystalline material such as white marble, reflects light diffusely with great efficiency. Many common materials exhibit a mixture of specular and diffuse reflection.
The visibility of objects, excluding light-emitting ones, is primarily caused by diffuse reflection of light: it is diffusely-scattered light that forms the image of the object in the observer's eye.

description_text:
Hover truck modeled in Blender 2.82. Works well in any real-time engines like UE4. Textures aren't the best, but head over to any free pbr texture website and find slightly rusty materials. All are included except a material in the truck bed. (all free just search free pbr materials). There are 3 boxes in the back that are all separate objects. Pictures rendered using Eevee (bloom, screen space reflections, ambient occlusion, and an HDRI from hdrihaven.com (canary warf) were enabled/used)The holographic sides were made using a checker texture from blender mixed with an emission and a transparent shader
The lettering on the sides are the cause of the majority of polygons, so If you want real low poly, just delete them

The set contains two types of elastic TPU breathing masks. It is possible to clamp any flat filter material with the different filter holder caps to the mask. Each mask has a lip sealing towards the face side and a exhaust valve which releases humidity. 
The masks where printed with a standard 3D Printer (see picture above) and TPU material. I used a 0,4mm / 0,6mm / and finally 0,8mm nozzle which gave me the best results. Also I had to modify some print parameters for TPU like the filament flow rate which was set to 120%.
Scalability of the masks: It is possible to scale the masks for a better fit. Dont forget to scale filter holder and valve with the same amount.
Washing: It is possible to put the TPU masks in boiling hot water or the dishwasher to desinfect them.
To seal the prints i used some layers of spray paint or better filler glue. You can check the sealing of the mask as well as the function of the valve if you put plastic foil instead of the filtermaterial. Also you can make a smoke test to see open spots.
The light version is easyer to print, for the heavy version support may be needed.
Have fun while printing and stay healthy and safe ;-)

what is PBR?Physically based rendering (PBR) is an approach in computer graphics that seeks to render graphics in a way that more accurately models the flow of light in the real world. Many PBR pipelines have the accurate simulation of photorealism as their goal. Feasible and quick approximations of the bidirectional reflectance distribution function and rendering equation are of mathematical importance in this field. Photogrammetry may be used to help discover and encode accurate optical properties of materials. Shaders may be used to implement PBR principles.Thanks to high performance and low costs of modern hardware it has become feasible to use PBR not only for industrial but also entertainment purposes wherever photorealistic images are desired including video games and movie making.A typical application provides an intuitive graphical user interface that allows artists to define and layer materials with arbitrary properties and to assign them to a given 2D or 3D object to recreate the appearance of any synthetic or organic material. Environments can be defined with procedural shaders or textures as well as procedural geometry or meshes or pointclouds. If possible all changes are made visible in real-time and therefore allow for quick iterations. Sophisticated applications allow savvy users to write custom shaders in a shading language.[Wikipedia]

Thanks to high performance and low costs of modern hardware it has become feasible to use PBR not only for industrial but also entertainment purposes wherever photorealistic images are desired including video games and movie making. A typical application provides an intuitive graphical user interface that allows artists to define and layer materials with arbitrary properties and to assign them to a given 2D or 3D object to recreate the appearance of any synthetic or organic material. Environments can be defined with procedural shaders or textures as well as procedural geometry or meshes or pointclouds. If possible all changes are made visible in real-time and therefore allow for quick iterations. Sophisticated applications allow savvy users to write custom shaders in a shading language. [Wikipedia]

description_text:
Black Hole
Simple model of a black hole similar to the one in the movie Interstellar (Gargantua) based on a tutorial by ShiveringCactus.
It is basically a black sphere and a (rotating) disk with some galaxy texture plus a refracting torus, which simulates the bending of the light behind by the strong gravity (gravity lens). I added an additional disk under the original one with a c4d galaxy shader to get some more twirly line structures around. For animation I just rotated these two disks together, which gives an impressive visual effect. By playing around with different transparency settings of the torus, e.g. inner reflection: on, You get different appearances. You can color filter the galaxy material to get even more different looks. Have fun!The images werde rendered in Cinema4D, the first image was edited in Photoshop to match better with the original.
Model is for CInema 4D, the galaxy texture image is filtered and it is used also in the alpha channel.
If You like the model please leave a like after downloading. Thank You! :-)

Made from CNC (Computer numerical control) bent steel wire, the fixture is available in a number of different finishesfrom black and white textured powder coat and decorative metal plating such as gold and Chrome. The fixture is illuminated by a energy efficient high output dim-able LED light source with a hight 91 CRI light quality and available in both warm and neutral white colour temperatures. Featuring a Opalescent hand blown white glass globe, while finished with a nylon braided electrical cord.

description_text:
Are you making a space game or perhaps something more fantasy oriented - Well why not add some glowing stones to your scenes. Change the emission map settings to make each iteration of this model unique by changing which cracks glow and by how much. By doing this you have complete control over your scene. The possibilities are endless! Your character will have so many unique glowing stones coming at them, they won't know what to do with them all.
Model Features:
Fully textured rock surface, completely custom made using Materialize so you can be sure that when you render your rocks your results will be stunning.
The model has custom texture files ranging for Diffuse, bump, metallic, normal, smoothness, edge AO and emisson maps so when you get up close an personal the thing looks out of this world.
The emission values have been linked to the dark regions (rock's cracks) of the diffuse map so with a few tweeks of the emission values your rock can be re-used saving the need to create a whole new model to create unique and complex scenes. Re-Use and Recycle the model over and over again! 
Realistic PBR textures used with a compact model design made to be universally game friendly.
Watch as the light eradiates from the rock's cracks using several directly applied 3D effects creating a different, stunning visual effect from every angle. Use in a dark scene and watch the cracks light up or perhaps use in a well lit scene and see a dubtle glow as you marvel at the realistic rock textures. the choice is up to you.
Available Formats:
Blender (Model's Native program made with version 2.8)
Obj/Mtl (Zipped in separate files)
fbx
dae
All file formats have been separately zipped along with the textures used. 
Please check out my other models for all your creative needs. I hope to be of service to your next creative project. :)

description_text: This is an industrial style lamp we design for our Laboratory in Milan. No one shared something similar in the Community, so we decided to project one big dimension lamp, but full optimized for 3D printing: NO support required, easy to print, solid and functional. It' not an easy target because usually the old lamps had a large cup, but we divided it in two to give a more interesting look with a six screw assembly, and to be able to generate the LampB file in spiralize the outer contour(light diffusion). In this way, you save a lot of time to print it. Please note you need two steel bars, the upper one with bolts, to hang safely the lamp to the cieling. You can see them in the last picture (the red ones) and in the pictures of the printed object. Diameter 8 mm. All the best! Print Settings Notes: Print all the parts with a big machine, 400x400 area. NO SUPPORT required! IMPORTANT: to create a solid object, print all with a 0.8 Nozzle size and 0.4 Layer high. It will be very sturdy. The Spiralized object is made in transparent PLA (big nozzle anyway) but it could be created in PETG or similar transparent filaments. Post-Printing After the printing, mount all the stuff with some parker screw or anything you like to give it an industrial look. Before to print, is better to paint and maybe give an antique finish to all the metallic parts. Use a simple electric wire and choose the kind of light you like.

description_text:
UPDATES ***  
7/6/14 - I've added a PDF Read Me guide (v.2) to using the adapter.  
6/16/14 - updated files to improve fit and reduce friction.  May be loose on some commercial canisters but will now fit CineStill film and possibly Kalt.  Print using 40% or 50% infill.  
***  
Tested and working. This adapts 35mm film for use in 120 medium format cameras.  By using this, you get full exposure of the film strip, sprocket holes and all.  This is designed to be a perfect copy of a 120 spool when the top and bottom parts are inserted onto a 35mm film canister.  Use an empty 120 spool for the takeup - it's easy to modify it by taping it to accept the 35mm film tail in the right place and make the slot thinner to grip the tail.    
The bottom part is printed as is.  The top part must first be rotated 180 about X or Y to sit flat on the bed for printing.  Recommend 40% infill (even 50% is ok) due to the small cross-section of the splines.  
Do not force adapters on.  Make sure the splines are aligned and if tight, trim/sand or wiggle on carefully.  The splines may need to be trimmed to fit Kalt bulk loading canisters and some others.  
The hole for viewing the film number (usually a red window) on the camera must be taped over with black gaffer's tape or some suitable opaque tape to avoid back side exposure of the film.  You will need to wind blindly about 1-1/2 turns at the beginning and taper down to 1 turn at the end.  Most medium format cameras have no rewind, so you will need to unload the film in a darkroom or changing bag and manually rewind the 35mm film back into its canister.  When processing, specify "process only" and "do not cut" and cut the film yourself.  
These were designed for the Flyer 6x6 camera developed as a result of the Pinhole Printed Kickstarter project (http://pinholeprinted.com) but can be used in any 120 medium format camera.  If you do not have a 3D printer or have it tied up with other things, you can order them from pinholeprinted.com and support the artist in future creations.  
This is CC by SA 3.0 - this means anyone can freely print or even sell the adapters - but you must provide attribution if you do so.  You can print a Thing Tag right off this page and display it if demonstrating your printer capabilities or distribute it with any copies you sell.

description_text: Thanks to 707 and SketchVC10. The Boeing 747SP is a modified version of the Boeing 747 jet airliner which was designed for ultra-long-range flights. The SP stands for "Special Performance". Compared with its predecessor, the 747-100, the 747SP retains its wide-body, four-engine layout, along with its double-deck design, but has a shortened fuselage, larger tailplane, and simplified trailing edge flaps. The weight saved by the shortened fuselage permits longer range and increased speed relative to other 747 configurations. Known during development as the short-body 747SB, the 747SP was designed to meet a 1973 joint request from Pan American World Airways and Iran Air, who were looking for a high-capacity airliner with sufficient range to cover Pan Am's New York–Middle Eastern routes and Iran Air's planned Tehran–New York route. The aircraft also was intended to provide Boeing with a mid-size wide-body airliner to compete with existing trijet airliners. The 747SP first entered service with Pan Am in 1976. The aircraft was later acquired by VIP and government customers. While in service, the 747SP set several aeronautical performance records, but sales did not meet the expected 200 units, and production ultimately totaled 45 aircraft.
